subject.title: Feature: config option to route gateway lifecycle warnings to a dedicated channel

question: Should OpenClaw add a general messages-level internal-warning destination/category router, and what categories/defaults should it support relative to existing suppression and channel-specific controls?
rationale: Source proves the capability is missing, but choosing a public config contract and diagnostic visibility semantics requires maintainer product direction because this changes warning delivery across channels and existing config surfaces.

options.title: Approve default-compatible router
options.body: Add an opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

options.title: Keep suppression-only controls
options.body: Treat messages.suppressToolErrors plus narrower channel fixes as the supported operator path and close or narrow routing requests after maintainer confirmation.

options.title: Split warning classes
options.body: Handle lifecycle, tool errors, cron, and session-maintenance warnings as separate issues instead of one shared router.

recommendation.title: Approve default-compatible router
recommendation.body: Add an opt-in router for lifecycle, tool-error, and system-notice warnings while preserving current active-channel behavior by default.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate from recent warning-policy and Telegram suppression history.
